newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool production seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool production seen falling.

text.p: The Australian Wool Production Forecasting Committee has reduced by four percent its estimate for 1995/96 production of Australian wool and also cut its forecast of 1996/97 production.
The latest estimate for 1995/96 (July-June) is 654.8 million kg and includes an increase in on-farm stocks of 14.0 million kg, the committee said in a statement.
A total of 146.0 million head of sheep were shorn in 1995/96 at an average cut per head of 4.48 kg, it said.
Opening flock numbers for 1995/96 were 123.2 million, it said.
The committee is forecasting 1996/97 production at 639.2 million kg within the range 625.0-655.0 million kg.
This is down from the 641.0 million kg forecast in June and represents a 2.4 percent decline from 1995/96.
The lower forecast reflects the changing flock structure with a higher proportion of ewes and lambs making up the 1996/97 opening numbers, it said.
